why: Maintainers report successful main CI fell from 23m16s to 14m10s median after moving critical workflows to Blacksmith, with median runner pickup falling from 82s to 16s.
Project write-up explains how trusted PRs use ephemeral RunsOn runners and links the change-based selective checks that trim the large test matrix.
A small test subset runs on each PR update. Bors runs the full suite in its merge queue and can combine approved PRs into a rollup.
A dedicated writer prewarms Cargo dependency caches used by PR jobs. Maintainers recorded 11.8–20.9 minutes for cold Rust setup and 0.7–3.4 minutes when warm.
The primary workflow uses a 58:42 Test Runner shard split on macOS and a large Linux runner for its Bun test job.
PR checks configure signed Turborepo Remote Cache. Wrangler and Miniflare tests are split into three shards on Windows and two on other platforms.
JS package CI runs build, test, and type checks with turbo --affected and uses an OIDC-backed remote task cache on same-repository PRs.
Main CI uses Blacksmith runners and path filters to select JS and Rust checks on PR updates, then validates the merge group.
The PR workflow sets up Bazel remote caching for framework unit and integration tests and remote build execution for DevTools.
Checks for affected Nx projects before running relevant checks and constructs a sharded end-to-end build matrix.
Isolates the Windows browser spec reported to consume about 28% of suite time and splits the remaining specs into two shards. Skips docs-only runs of these tests.
The small Bazel rules repo uses Aspect Cloud and configures a Bazel remote cache for eligible PR jobs with credentials.
The test workflow uses 16-vCPU Depot Linux runners and Namespace macOS and Windows runners. Windows tests run in three partitions with a shared Rust cache key.
Restores warmed Cargo build artifacts across OS jobs, checks manifest resolution early, and cancels superseded PR runs.
PR tests use Namespace runners and a shared sccache bucket, with event-specific test selection for pull requests and merge groups.
The blocking PR workflow splits its Bazel Windows tests across four runners and avoids duplicate cache uploads from all shards.
Runs core PR checks on Namespace profiles, keeps Cargo cache-key inputs consistent across jobs, and cancels superseded PR runs.
Path filters determine which build and test jobs to run, with Namespace runners for Linux and macOS jobs and a separate merge-group trigger.
A pre-build diff check skips build work for docs-only changes and skips Deno Core tests on irrelevant changes. The workflow shards integration tests.
Uses cargo-nextest for Rust tests and path-gates the VS Code extension jobs on TypeScript changes.
Runs Linux checks for PR feedback via clippy_pr.yml and adds the broader cross-platform test jobs in its dedicated merge-queue workflow.
The template engine reuses Cargo build caches across its parallel feature, compatibility, and integration test jobs.
Cancels superseded runs, restores cached Rust build state across jobs, and uses nextest for its own test suite.
The build matrix reserves selected Windows and macOS combinations for merge groups and cancels superseded pull-request runs.
The web framework caches Cargo build state across jobs and runs feature, compatibility, and lint checks in parallel.
A change-detection job separates docs and code checks. Test and build jobs consume its outputs, and newer PR runs cancel older ones.
Builds a package once and shares the artifact across the test matrix, which includes xdist jobs. Superseded PR runs are cancelled.
The small plugin builds a wheel once for the Python and pytest compatibility matrix and cancels older runs of the same PR.
Gates the full wheel matrix behind main, tags, or a full-build PR label and uses sccache for the Linux wheel job outside releases.
Path filters gate the PR test matrix on source and test changes, and jobs enable the uv dependency cache.
The small packaging library detects changed paths before scheduling pytest, type checks, or documentation checks.
Path-gates checks, runs slow Windows tests in three stable-hash shards, and uses xdist work stealing within each shard to shorten the tail.
Skips the test fan-out for docs-only changes and runs the code suites in parallel, including three separate web test jobs.
The PR test workflow ignores documentation-only changes, cancels superseded runs, and caches pip installs keyed to test requirements.
PR CI populates a Go module cache once for reuse across jobs, splits Go tests by platform and shard, and handles merge-group runs.
Backend Go tests are partitioned across jobs using the repo's package sharding script, with superseded PR runs cancelled.
Contributor docs describe automatic short smoke tests and explicitly triggered platform suites, and explain how CI selects affected Ginkgo tests.
Computes affected Go modules plus their transitive dependents for test jobs. Lint uses only directly changed modules, and an empty scope skips both.
Keys Go caches across module checksums, caches the internal tools separately, and splits race, tool, and compatibility tests across jobs.
The Go client caches by go.sum, spreads the supported Go-version matrix across native OS runners, and cancels stale PR jobs.
Caches npm and Elm dependencies and builds the UI once, sharing its dist artifact across the parallel cross-platform build jobs.
The small Go library's PR workflow delegates to Charm's cache-enabled Go build and test workflow and skips the examples build on Dependabot updates.
The small ASGI library enables uv caching and runs its Python compatibility test matrix in parallel.
